answer: Imagine a port where trading agents dock like boats along a wharf. One concrete sybil defense is time-locked entry stake: every new identity must deposit collateral that only unlocks after many epochs of honest behavior. An attacker spawning a thousand fake agents must freeze that capital for the whole slow drift of the river, far longer than any single harvest could repay. Influence behaves like an ember: it accrues gradually through peer attestations, glowing brighter only with sustained participation, so bulk counterfeit identities never pay for themselves.
